title: QA run · integration-system (FULL area) · 92f26f75 · 2026-08-11 · 5 PASS / 5 PARTIAL / 3 FAIL
body:
Full `integration-system` area run of the `checklist-test` skill — all **13 items** driven against a live showcase across 3 opus subagents, each on its own port + file DB. Text-only per RUNNER.md.

**Result: 5 PASS · 5 PARTIAL · 3 FAIL.**

> ⚠️ **One security-sensitive finding from this area is NOT described here.** It surfaced as an adjacent observation during `webhook-lifecycle` and was delivered privately as **`FOLLOW-UPS.md` D12**, per the maintainer ruling recorded on #7463. It does not change that item's passing verdict.

**Environment** — framework `92f26f75`/`f268b2b2` (branch `claude/platform-test-checklist-ocwugl`) · console bundle `09987b680` (`packages/console/dist/.objectui-sha`) · showcase app · isolated port + file DB per batch · scratch app copies in `/tmp` for every mutated-metadata boot (**no repo file was written at any point**).

## ✅ PASS — 5 items

- **`connector-stdio-default-deny`** (4/4 + both negatives) — the strongest security result of the area, and it is proven by **non-spawn**, not by an error message. The runner instrumented the fixture to append to a marker file on start: the marker appears on the allowlisted boot and is **absent on both deny boots**. All four variants covered — policy absent → boot aborts with the #3055/ADR-0024 message; allowlist `['node']` + `python3` → refused naming both the command **and** the configured allowlist (strict equality, no prefix/glob); allowlisted → materializes and dispatches; http transports **not** subject to the policy (0 `declarativeStdio` hits, degrades on unreachability instead). The refusal is fatal-at-start, never a degraded husk retrying toward an unauthorized process. Pin re-run 13/13.
- **`connector-descriptor-audit`** (3/3 + both negatives) — the inert-descriptor warning names the offender and prescribes both fixes; it is quiet for `enabled:false` and quiet when a same-name **runtime** registration exists — proven with a **discriminating** test, since the same audit pass named the *other* connector, making the silence attributable. Never fires for provider-bound instances across ~12 boots. Fires in-process on `metadata:reloaded` with no restart. Pin 9/9.
- **`webhook-lifecycle`** (6/6 + all three negatives) — declared webhooks materialize with both spec remaps; all three per-record variants deliver to a **local receiver**, each keyed by its own event. Bulk-vs-per-record separation proven with two subscribers on the **same object**: a predicate flow produced **exactly 2** aggregate-shaped deliveries (`matched:1` / `matched:2`, no `recordId`) on the bulk path and **zero** on the per-record path, with a control create afterwards proving that subscription was alive. **HMAC recomputed by hand** from the raw body → exact match. Authored `timeoutMs` enforced; a 404 target goes straight to `dead`; an unreachable port retries per the backoff ladder with every attempt durable. #3196 drift-guard verified by inserting legacy-shaped rows directly into the runner's own DB — the enqueuer warns **every cycle**, naming the bad trigger and that the row *"is dead while looking armed in Setup"*. #3197 confirmed: connector-attached webhooks are never read at registration.
- **`notify-inbox-delivery`** (5/5 + both negatives) — scoping is **server-side** (a third member's authenticated listing is empty; `sys_inbox_message` carries only the assignee's `user_id`). The 501 capability-unavailable envelope was proven on a **real messaging-less boot**, not asserted. An unregistered channel **dead-letters honestly** (`status:'dead'`, `error: "channel 'push' not registered"`) with no inbox row and no receipt.
- **`notification-preference-suppression`** (5/5 + both negatives) — suppression is a genuine drop with a located log line and `acted=0`; the reversal restores delivery. **Precedence proven with a control**: a `user_id='*'` row does suppress (a persona with no specific row got nothing) while the user-specific row overrides it. The **mandatory-topic bypass** was proven by booting a scratch config with `MessagingServicePlugin({mandatoryTopics:['task.assigned']})` mounted explicitly — the CLI never sets it — and the row landed despite an `enabled:false` preference.

## 🔴 FAIL — 3 items

### 1. `email-template-render` — three defects, none of them stale-dist

All three are **identical in `src`, in the `dist` the server executes, and on `origin/main`**.

**(a) A declared i18n bundle collides — only the last locale survives.** A stack declaring two `emailTemplates` with the same `name` and different `locale` logs `[Registry] Overwriting email_template: <pkg>:<name>` and materializes 3 of 4 authored templates; the en-US twin is gone. **Root cause:** `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (~line 1826) keys items `${packageId}:${baseName}` — **locale is not part of the key**. This contradicts the spec's own statement that *"multiple rows with the same name but different locale form an i18n bundle"*.

**(b) A no-locale `sendTemplate` renders an arbitrary locale.** With a bundle present as rows, calling `sendTemplate` with **no** `locale` rendered the **zh-CN** row — on two consecutive fresh boots — instead of the documented en-US default. **Root cause:** `plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts` (~line 548) `templateLoader.load()` queries `{name}` with `limit:1` and **no ordering** when locale is undefined, and `email-service.ts` (~line 1121) applies the en-US fallback **only when `preferred` was set**. Explicit locales resolve correctly (`zh-CN` exact; `fr-FR` and `en-GB` fall back to en-US); language-only `zh` does not prefix-match.

**(c) A runtime metadata write never materializes without a restart.** `PUT /api/v1/meta/email_template/<name>` → 200 and `[Registry] Registered email_template`, but the row never reaches `sys_email_template` — and **neither** of the subscription's own log lines fires (0 occurrences of "materialized from a runtime write", 0 of "runtime email-template sync failed"), so the callback registered at `email-plugin.ts` ~line 968 never runs, even though its boot line *"subscribed to email_template metadata changes"* is present. **Decisive control:** restarting on the same DB materializes it immediately (`{seeded:1, skipped:1}`) — so the bridge handles the item fine and only the **live event path** is dead. The plugin's own comment names this as the live path ("Studio saves / PUT /meta land as added/changed events").

_The rest of the item passes: rendering with every hole substituted and zero placeholder residue across ~12 sends; a missing **required** variable throws `MISSING_VARIABLES: title` with 0 messages reaching the transport while a missing **optional** one renders empty; `TEMPLATE_INACTIVE` withdrawal works and is reversible; from/replyTo overrides land with a control proving the default; the authoring-schema aliases all prescribe the right slot (`content`→`bodyHtml`, `from`→`fromOverride`, `title`→`subject`) while a non-alias gets no bogus suggestion; and the raw `/email/send` door answers 200 / 401 / 400 / 501 correctly, never a 500 for caller-fixable input. #4509 false compliance does **not** reproduce — an admin edit takes effect on the very next send._

### 2. `job-scheduled-run` — job timeouts are not enforced in the durable record

**Reproduction rule** — declare a job with `timeout: 2000` whose handler sleeps 10 s; let it fire; read `sys_job_run` and `sys_job`.
**Expected** run status `timeout`, counted as a failure (per `JobExecutionStatus`/#3494).
**Actual** every row is `status: 'success'` with `duration_ms` 10025 / 10003 / 10001 / 10004 — **five times the declared timeout** — and `sys_job` reads `last_status: success`, `failure_count: 0`.

The scheduler **does** abandon and retry: a `retryPolicy` variant fired attempt 2 at timeout+backoff (+2.5 s). Yet **both** attempts still landed as `success` rows.

**Root cause (read in the running dist, re-checked against the newer src — identical).** `DbJobAdapter.schedule()` passes its recording wrapper **into** `IntervalJobAdapter`/`CronJobAdapter` as the handler, so `runWithPolicy`'s `Promise.race` timeout guard wraps the **recorder** instead of the other way round. When the guard rejects, the recorder is still awaiting the un-cancellable handler; when that finally resolves, `wrap()` writes `finishRun(runId,'success')`.

**Why the pin stayed green:** the `timeout` status the adapters *do* compute lives only in the **in-memory `JobExecution` list that `sys_job_run` never reads** — so `interval-job-adapter.test.ts`'s *"enforces a per-attempt timeout and records status 'timeout'"* passes against the in-memory adapter while the persisted truth an operator sees says success. The same seam explains `sys_job_run.attempt` being hardcoded to 1 for every retry (and each retry inflating `run_count`).

_Everything else passes: all three schedule variants verified by their **own** run row **and** side-effect tick file (interval to the ms, cron exactly on the minute, once at the declared instant); upsert-by-name holds across restarts; retry backoff measured exactly (1000 ms then 2000 ms); the policy-less probe ran **once**, confirming the 17.0.0 `maxRetries` default of 0 (#4661), not the old 3; both skip doors are loud and distinct; runtime job creation is refused 403 `NOT_CREATABLE` (#4509 door closed)._

### 3. `external-datasource-federated-read` — the federated read returns nothing

**Reproduction rule** — on a stock boot: `GET /api/v1/datasources/showcase_external/remote-tables` → 200 listing `customers`(7 cols) + `orders`(7 cols); then `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_ext_customer`.
**Expected** the 3 fixture rows. **Actual** 200 `{"records":[],"total":0}`; by-id → 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. Reproduced on two boots with fresh DBs.

The remote SQLite genuinely holds 3 customers and 4 orders (read directly **and** via the platform's own introspection route). A filter on a **non-existent column** also returns 200 empty rather than a driver error — **proof the read never reaches the external SQL driver at all**.

**Suspected root cause (boot ordering).** `No driver available for object, skipping schema sync {"object":"showcase_ext_customer"}` is logged at 09:38:37.014, while `Registered driver {"driverName":"showcase_external"}` and `Auto-connected declared datasources` only happen at **09:38:38.413** — so ObjectQLPlugin's federated branch (`plugin.ts:1136-1152`, the `SqlDriver.registerExternalObject` call that installs the object→remote-table mapping) never runs, leaving the query path with no binding.

**Second, separately actionable hazard** found on a control boot where the mapping *did* register: the platform injects its org-scoping predicate onto a federated remote table that has no such column — `select * from \`customers\` where (\`organization_id\` = '…' or \`organization_id\` is null)`.

**Also failing (clause 1):** the write refusal is **correct server-side** — `ExternalWriteForbiddenError` names the datasource, its `schemaMode`, and both flags that would be required — but reaches the client as a bare **500 INTERNAL_ERROR**, indistinguishable from a crash. _Nothing was applied: the remote table is byte-identical after both attempts._

## 🟡 PARTIAL — 5 items

### The connector trio, and one cause behind three partials

`connector-declarative-boot`, `connector-degraded-recovery` and `connector-spec-path-no-escape` each pass their substance and each carry the **same** unproven half.

What is proven: all three provider variants materialize with actions derived exactly from the upstream; all three malformed authoring shapes are refused by the **real build gate** with located ADR-0097 messages; an unknown provider key **aborts boot with rollback**, listing the installed providers. A dead upstream **degrades without taking the boot down**, stays visible as a husk with its reason, fails dispatch **fast** (31 ms) quoting that reason verbatim, and **recovers restart-free** — proven from one continuous boot log (zero shutdown lines) after restoring the upstream file. Backoff doubling was measured exactly (5.07 / 10.11 / 20.19 s). Operational and configuration faults are correctly split. Path confinement was tested with a **canary**: the out-of-root target was a *valid* OpenAPI document whose `operationId` would have materialized a working action had the guard leaked — across absolute, `../` and embedded `../../../../` probes, the connector never materialized and the canary appears **0 times** in every boot log; the check is on the **resolved** path, and a path resolving back inside the root is accepted.

**The shared gap: the dev metadata reload does not re-ingest connector items.** `reconcileDeclaredConnectors` reads `ql.registry.listItems('connector')`, and the artifact reload re-ingests object definitions but **not** connector items — so a connector edit on disk fires a reload with no reconcile, no teardown, no re-materialize. Not scored as a fail: the default `os dev` restarts the serve child on recompile, so the user-visible loop does apply the change, and the production trigger (a Studio package publish) was not drivable here. **Flagged for triage.** _Also unproven: the 300 s backoff ceiling (the runner stopped at the 40 s cycle rather than wait ~10 min) and "a config edit resets the backoff" — a reload does force an early retry but **advances** the backoff rather than resetting it, matching the source, where only a signature change resets._

### `datasource-admin-lifecycle`

**Secret handling is exemplary** and worth calling out next to D12: `hasSecret` is a boolean with no value in list or detail, **and** a byte-level scan of every table and column of the running DB found **no occurrence** of the inline secret — it is split out server-side and never lands in the persisted draft. Refusals attribute to their own service (`DATASOURCE_ADMIN_ERROR` vs `EXTERNAL_DATASOURCE_ERROR`), so the #4249 mis-attribution is absent.

`partial` solely because clause 4 is `blocked(fixture)` exactly as the item's own `knownGaps` pre-authorises — `os dev` wires `ExternalDatasourceServicePlugin` by default, so the 503 cannot be provoked. **Confirms D6**: the admin CRUD routes actually mounted carry **no route-ledger entry** (the ledger's five datasource entries are all federation ones, and the ledgered `/external/tables` spelling differs from the live `/remote-tables`) — the tranche-3 gap stands. **Observation:** a draft naming an *unknown* driver is **accepted 201** with `status:'error'` rather than refused — health reporting rather than validation.

### `flow-connector-picker`

The picker follows the **runtime registry**, not the metadata list: its five options diff name-by-name against `GET /automation/connectors`, and it correctly does **not** offer `showcase_erp_catalog` — the catalog descriptor that `GET /meta/connector` *does* list — so it cannot wire an undispatchable node. Provenance annotation is exact. Actions are derived end-to-end.

**`partial`: action input schemas are not surfaced.** After committing an action, the Input section stays a generic untyped key/value repeater, with no field derived from the descriptor's `inputSchema`. `git grep inputSchema` over `app-shell` at the **served** pin **and** on `origin/main` hits only `default-schemas.ts` — nothing consumes it, so this is not fixed upstream.

## Notes worth keeping

1. **Seed-data trap in the notify path:** the stock seed assigns `ada@`/`linus@`/`sam@example.com`, which are **not `sys_user` rows** and resolve verbatim to non-users — so a **stock** reassignment lands an inbox row nobody can read. The runner signed up real personas and used their emails instead.
2. **`POST /api/v1/data/sys_account` now answers 405** (create not allowed), so the previously-used recipe for turning a seeded demo persona into a real login is closed on this build.
3. **A flow authored over the metadata API is not editable in Studio** — with or without `?package=`, it opens behind "This flow is provided by an installed package, so it is read-only at runtime", because `ResourceEditPage` treats an item as artifact-backed when `layered.code != null && _packageId !== 'sys_metadata'` and `flow` declares `allowOrgOverride:false`. The editable path is the console's own create page.
4. **Checklist slip** — `email-template-render` clause 7 names a `{to, subject, bodyHtml}` message body; the wire keys are `html`/`text` (`bodyHtml` is the **template** field). The literal shape the clause names is refused 400 "at least one of text or html is required".
5. **Predicate (`multi:true`) writes are unreachable over REST by design** (#3897 strips `options.multi` from the batch routes), so the bulk-webhook clause needs a flow `update_record`/`delete_record` node with `multi:true` fired through the api trigger — recorded so the next sweep does not re-derive it.
6. **Notification observation:** the `['push']` probe's flow-run summary reports `status:'success', acted:1` while nothing was delivered. The dead-letter is visible in `sys_notification_delivery` but not in the run summary.
